title: The Telegram allowlist tests require allow-all when both lists are empty and accept a message when only the sender or only the channel matches, so they encode the registered S1 (Telegram allowlist is allow-all unless both lists are set) as the required behaviour

evidence.note: "allows message when sender is whitelisted (OR logic)"
"allows message when channel is whitelisted (OR logic)"
"allows all when both whitelist env vars are empty"

sibling_sites_checked: Other unit tests of inbound Telegram trust: none (preflight/crossEnvRules checks the five Telegram keys are set together, not the allowlist). alphaDrop is mocked here.
severity_rationale: S2: the test locks in the behaviour that lets any Telegram sender trigger a buy (the S1 AUD-BUY-006); fixing the defect will turn these cases red by design, which is the point to record for Phase 28.
recommendation: Phase 28 (with the Phase 24 decision on AUD-BUY-006): rewrite the cases to the chosen rule (fail closed when the lists are empty, require the configured combination) and add a case that an unlisted sender in a listed channel is rejected if that is the decision.
affected_cases: allows message when sender is whitelisted (OR logic)
allows message when channel is whitelisted (OR logic)
allows all when both whitelist env vars are empty
escaped_regression: Today's code already escapes (AUD-BUY-006): with TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_SENDERS and TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_CHANNELS empty every message is routed to the buy handler, and the third case requires exactly that.
